newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX index hits 5th successive high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX index hits 5th successive high.

text.p: The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange extended this week's gains to reach a new all-time high on Thursday as oil company MOL continued to lead the market, traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,728.58 points, up 12.16 points, closing at the fifth successive new high.
Expectations for an energy price increase, effective from January 1, may be behind MOL's continuous rise, traders said.

"Prime Minister Gyula Horn said 23 percent and if they start out from this level in a bargaining position, they might agree at around 27 to 28 percent," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities. "This may be one reason behind the buyings."

Earlier this month Horn said energy prices would probably be raised by up to 23 percent. The government has not said how big a rise it planned, but press reports said it was between 30 and 40 percent.
MOL rose to 1,820 forints before retreating to finish at 1,805 forints, up 30.
The oil company's share contributed 446.6 million forints to the day's spot share turnover of 1.47 billion forints.
Other key shares traded rangebound and in some cases investors decided to sell with the aim of profit-taking.

"OTP declined, I felt some profit-taking in this case," Agoston said. Investors, having bought the paper at between 2,400 and 2,500 forints, decided to sell as the share has apparently reached a resistance level.
OTP peaked at 2,725 forints, before retreating to close at 2,670, down 55.
Although the BUX index still rose today the pace of rise slowed down and traders said the market needed fresh information to trigger substantial changes.
"We have reached a level where no major changes can be expected until fresh news come out," Agoston said.
"Two major developments can be expected, one is that Moody's and S&P examines Hungary's rating," he said, adding they might upgrade Hungary's rating to an investment grade.
The other will be the new batch of corporate results which Agoston expected to be generally good.
In the listed A category of the bourse (formerly called listed category) companies will start to release figures later this month with a November 15 deadline.
